title: BNCI 2020-001 Reach-and-Grasp Electrode Comparison EEG dataset
description: EEG recordings from healthy participants performing self-initiated palmar and lateral reach-and-grasp actions, acquired with three systems: gel-based laboratory EEG, water-based mobile EEG, and dry-electrode mobile EEG. The dataset supports study of the feasibility of decoding natural reach-and-grasp movement-related cortical potentials across acquisition modalities for brain-computer interfaces. The primary publication is Schwarz et al. (2020), Frontiers in Neuroscience (10.3389/fnins.2020.00849). It is distributed in BIDS format through the MOABB benchmark collection; the 2020 International BCI Competition review (10.3389/fnhum.2022.898300) is a related reference, not the data paper.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 256 Hz from 58 EEG and 6 EOG channels in a 5% grid montage using g.tec USBamp/g.Ladybird (gel), EEG-Versatile (water) and EEG-Hero (dry) systems. Participants performed 80 self-initiated palmar and lateral grasp trials each. Online filtering used a Chebyshev 0.01-100 Hz band and a 50 Hz notch. Offline preprocessing included 0.3-60 Hz Butterworth filtering, infomax ICA (gel and water systems only), amplitude thresholding, and joint probability/kurtosis rejection.
